Try Playscapes – a new global playground map
How accessible are playgrounds in the world’s cities? Where do children have safe, nearby places to play, move, and meet friends – and where are such spaces missing altogether? A new web-based platform called Playscapes now makes it possible to explore these questions in detail. Developed by researchers at the University of Southern Denmark, the Swedish consultancy Spacescape, and web design firm OAWA, Playscapes allows users to compare playground access across cities worldwide — from a global overview down to the neighborhood level. The tool is freely available to try at playgroundresearch.org/playscapes . It is currently a beta-version for testing, and we kindly ask everyone who tests it for feedback.

architecture_steps.title: Video Observation
architecture_steps.body: A real-world video is sampled into frames and keyframes to make human behavior searchable.

architecture_steps.title: ML Interaction Extraction
architecture_steps.body: YOLO detects children and space elements, SAM segments them, and CLIP filters for meaningful interaction scenes.

architecture_steps.title: Reference Data Scraping
architecture_steps.body: Public playground and spatial-access datasets are collected from OpenStreetMap and reference articles.

architecture_steps.title: Vectorisation + Comparison
architecture_steps.body: Image evidence keeps CLIP vectors while scraped text and dataset summaries are vectorised with CountVectorizer and TF-IDF.

architecture_steps.title: Design Rule Synthesis
architecture_steps.body: The mock API layer converts evidence into taxonomy-specific geometry, material, interaction, and color rules.

architecture_steps.title: Fragment Rendering + Export
architecture_steps.body: The system renders fragment families, then exports Blender-ready JSON and CSV packages for downstream modeling.

mock_rules.geometry_rule: repeat narrow vertical ribs and offset every third panel
mock_rules.material_rule: use perforated metal or translucent acrylic panels
mock_rules.interaction_rule: keep apertures at child-eye level and alternate dense/open zones
mock_rules.color_rule: lean toward saturated warning tones with one bright accent
